newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa sets out position on EU trade talks.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa sets out position on EU trade talks.

text.p: South Africa on Friday outlined its long-awaited negotiating position in trade talks with the European Union, handing over its "mandate" during a meeting with EU officials in Pretoria.

"We met this morning with the EU representative here and handed over a document on South Africa's basis for negotiations on a trade and development agreement," Department of Trade and Industry director of trade relations Bahle Sibisi said by telephone from Pretoria.
The move paves the way for the resumption of formal negotiations between the two sides in South Africa at the end of next month, he said.

Sibisi declined to detail South Africa's position but said the negotiating document was the culmination of extensive consultation with South African business, labour, parliamentary and public interests.
It also took into account comments from South Africa's neighbours in the South African Customs Union and the Southern African Development Community.

Other members of the five-nation customs union -- Botswana, Namibia, Lesotho and Swaziland -- have expressed concern that a free trade agreement between Pretoria and Brussels could cost them millions in lost customs revenues.
